advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the recurring-alert exemption robust to a configurable bot identity (match by tag e.g. `binding-drift-alert`, or by the BRIDGE_BOT_NAME value, not a hardcoded author string).
evidence: docs/jira-sync-setup.md:154 lists BRIDGE_BOT_NAME as an operator-settable variable with default `rebar-bridge[bot]`
Ticket comment: 'Recurring alert filings always collide by title ... Detector A needs an exemption path — by author, by tag, or by an explicit recurring-filing marker.'
advisory.finding: The recurring-alert exemption hardcodes the author string "rebar-bridge[bot]", but that identity is a configurable CI variable (vars.BRIDGE_BOT_NAME with a fallback default). If an operator sets a custom BRIDGE_BOT_NAME, the exemption silently stops matching and the recurring [binding-drift] bridge-fsck filings are re-counted as duplicates — the exact false-positive the ticket's precision requirement demanded be suppressed.
scenarios: An operator overrides vars.BRIDGE_BOT_NAME to a custom name; the canary-filed [binding-drift] alerts then carry that author and are no longer exempt, so the rolling-hour duplicate count includes them and can trip a false alarm.
advisory.suggested_fix: Prefer the ticket's tag-based exemption (`binding-drift-alert` tag applied by canary_bridge.py) or read the configured bot name, rather than string-equal on "rebar-bridge[bot]".

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Skip records whose normalized title is empty in the duplicate-title aggregation so title-less creations are not grouped as collisions.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/recent_creates.py:57: `return " ".join(_NON_ALNUM.sub(" ", title.lower()).split())` — for input "" (or all-punctuation) yields ""
ABSENCE: no guard skips empty/blank normalized titles before grouping in `_duplicate_records`/`_peak_duplicate_excess`.
advisory.finding: normalize_title("") returns the empty string, so any CREATE events with a missing, empty, or punctuation/whitespace-only title all normalize to "" and are grouped together as same-title duplicates, potentially producing a spurious duplicate-title alarm from title-less creations that are not real title collisions.
scenarios: A burst of CREATE events lacking titles (or with punctuation-only titles) all map to the empty normalized key and inflate the duplicate-excess count within a rolling hour.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a duplicate_title_peak_hour test with duplicates spanning more than one rolling hour to exercise the window-eviction (delta=-1) path and assert peak decays.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:428 `while start < len(records) and records[start][0] < cutoff:` then line 430 `excess += _adjust_group(groups, old_title_norm, old_impact, -1)`
All four duplicate tests use timestamps `2026-02-01T00:0{index}:00` / `00:{index:02d}:00`, all within one hour, so the eviction branch never runs.
create_volume_peak_hour has an explicit 'alarms_and_clears' test (line 195) but duplicate_title_peak_hour has no analogous window-clears test.
advisory.finding: The duplicate-title sliding-window eviction path (_adjust_group with delta=-1 and group deletion) is never exercised: all duplicate_title_peak_hour tests place CREATE events within a single hour so `start` never advances past a duplicate while it is still in the window. A regression that broke the decrement/eviction (e.g. never subtracting excess, or failing to delete the emptied group) would not be caught for the duplicate metric.
scenarios: Duplicates spread across >1 hour so the peak excess should decay as events age out.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: N duplicate-title CREATEs at 00:00, 02:00, 04:00 (each >1h apart) and assert peak_hour reflects only concurrent duplicates, not the cumulative total.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where two same-title tickets have the SAME single-file impact path and assert peak_hour == 1 (not suppressed).
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:382 `if group["unknown"] == 0 and len(group["impacts"]) == count:` return 0 (suppress)
test_duplicate_title_peak_hour_suppresses_distinct_file_impact uses distinct paths `src/pkg/__init__.py` and `src/pkg/_init.py` (line 139), never the same path.
ABSENCE: no test where two duplicate-title tickets share one impact path (impacts dict has 1 key, count 2) to confirm it is NOT suppressed.
advisory.finding: Suppression only tests DISTINCT file-impact paths; there is no test that two same-normalized-title tickets with the SAME single-file impact path are still counted as a duplicate. The suppression guard is `len(group['impacts']) == count` — if impacts collapse to one key it must NOT suppress, but no test asserts this.
scenarios: Two same-title tickets both touching the same single file — a genuine duplicate that must still count.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where [binding-drift]-titled duplicates come from a non-bridge author and assert they are counted (not exempted).
evidence: test_duplicate_title_peak_hour_exempts_recurring_bridge_alerts sets author='rebar-bridge[bot]' for all 12 events (line 168); no negative case with a matching title but a different author.
advisory.finding: The author gate in _recurring_alert_create is untested: the exemption requires BOTH author == 'rebar-bridge[bot]' AND a '[binding-drift]' title, but only the both-true case is tested. A '[binding-drift]' title from a non-bridge author (should NOT be exempt) has no test, so dropping the author condition would not fail any test.
scenarios: A non-bridge author mass-files [binding-drift]-titled tickets — should still alarm as duplicates.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Deduplicate CREATE events per ticket (or count creations per ticket-id rather than per event file) so a retired+active CREATE pair is not double-counted.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/event_metrics.py:69-93: `_event_files` returns both active `-CREATE.json` and non-active `-CREATE.json.retired` files
src/rebar/_store/sync.py:235 references `*.retired` as regenerable compaction leftovers, confirming retired tombstones can coexist with active files
dropped.finding: _create_events reads CREATE event files with include_retired=True, so a ticket whose genesis CREATE has been compacted to a *.json.retired tombstone AND also has an active CREATE file would be counted twice, double-counting a single creation in both the volume metric and (when impacts are not distinct) the duplicate metric.
scenarios: During/after compaction a ticket has both an active and a retired CREATE file; the volume peak-hour counts both, inflating the CREATE-rate signal and risking a false volume alarm.
